summary: AE + SE walked FinSight through Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs to diagnose recent inference failures. Customer interested in pilot to run their request logs and validate latency/cost tradeoffs and security posture.
transcript:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (FinSight), Sana Patel (FinSight Eng Mgr), Jordan Kim (FinSight Security), Ava Torres (FinSight DE)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Rivera from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Priya Shah, our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:05 Marcus: Good thanks, Alex. Excited to see the tracing stuff. We had some weird error spikes last week.
00:12 Priya: Great, we'll jump into the console and show tracing, request logs, and how to debug those spikes. First quick agenda: walk tracing UI, error analysis flows, request log drill-downs, and then open Q&A.
00:22 Sana: Sounds good. Our main asks: can we see per-request latency breakdowns, which part of the stack is slow (network, KV cache, model inference), and is there an easy way to correlate with errors?
00:30 Priya: Yep. We'll demo the latency waterfall, the KV cache hit/miss markers (sometimes transcribed as K V cache), and the error analysis which links to stack traces and input payloads.
00:42 Alex: Quick qual — can you remind us of your current stack and where models are hosted?
00:47 Marcus: We're on-prem for the data plane, but cloud control plane. Models are hosted in our GCP project using a mix of internal endpoints and some open models. We also run a small NIMBUS cluster — uh, sorry, Nimbus, I mean — on-prem for sensitive workloads.
00:58 Jordan: Security context — we need audit logs, SSO/SAML config, and KMS integration. Also data residency questions.
01:05 Alex: Understood. We'll attach SOC 2 and the network diagram as follow-ups. Priya, demo time?
01:12 Priya: Sure. Sharing my screen — navigating to the Console -> Tracing. Here's the timeline view. You can see spikes at ~14:30 UTC last Wed, which matches the incident.
01:28 Priya: The trace shows a long tail in the 'model_inference' span, about 3200ms at peak. There's also intermittent 'kv-cache fetch' steps that show 120ms for misses. Note: sometimes the auto transcript says K V cache and it reads weird.
01:45 Sana: Can you filter by model version? We had a rollout to v3.1-quant last Tuesday.
01:52 Priya: Yep filtering now — okay with v3.1-quant, the traces cluster differently: more frequent short tails but occasional 3s spikes. That suggests a kernel scheduling issue on GPUs for that quantized variant.
02:05 Marcus: Is there a way to correlate GPU utilization or infra metrics to the trace?
02:12 Priya: Yes, we link traces to infra metrics and request logs. If you click 'Related Metrics' it brings up GPU pod CPU/GPU util, memory, and the serving lane. See here — during the spikes, GPU utilization was saturated on one worker and autoscaler didn't kick fast enough due to policy settings.
02:30 Alex: That's where Dedicated vs Hosted conversation comes in — dedicated pools can give predictable throughput. But I know you prefer on-prem for PII.
02:40 Marcus: For sensitive data we want Private (VPC/on-prem). Can Redwood run the control plane while we host the data plane?
02:48 Alex: Absolutely — our Private deployment supports customer-managed data plane with our control plane or fully on-prem depending on needs.
02:55 Jordan: For KMS/HSM, do you integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS? Also do you support customer HSM?
03:03 Priya: Yes to both; we support AWS/GCP KMS and can integrate HSM. We'll include the certs and a short integration note in the follow-up pack.
03:12 Sana: Back to request logs — we sometimes have redactions; can we keep sampled payloads but strip PII?
03:18 Priya: Console supports redaction rules and tokenization. You can configure sampling rate and pseudonymization. Also request logs are linked to trace IDs so you can replay the payloads in a safe environment.
03:30 Alex: Now I'll show error analysis. Here is the error explorer — you can group by error type, message, and stack hash.
03:42 Priya: We'll click into an error group — this one is a 'model_timeout' with 504s. The error page lists top n failing request examples and shows the input tokens and a diff view for similar requests. The transcript often mashes words, e.g., "model time out" or "model time out" but the UI shows raw logs.
04:05 Marcus: Can we attach our internal correlation ID? We have a request_id header.
04:10 Priya: Yes, you can push custom headers and Redwood will index them; you can search and pivot on any custom field.
04:18 Ava: Is there an API to export request logs for internal analysis?
04:22 Alex: Yep. We have a request logs export API and S3 sink options, plus Kafka connector for streaming.
04:30 Marcus: About cost — quantized models saved us cost but may have higher variance in latency. Can Redwood Optimize suggest quantization profiles?
04:38 Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization/bitwidth per workload and we can show expected unit cost vs p99 latency tradeoffs. We'll prepare a short simulation for your traffic.
04:50 Jordan: For audits, can we get immutable audit logs and retention controls?
04:55 Alex: Yes, audit logs are immutable and we can set retention policies per customer. We'll include retention SLAs in the docs.
05:05 Sana: Can we run a pilot where Redwood ingests 1 week of request logs and runs the tracing/analysis on them? That would prove the hypothesis.
05:12 Alex: That's the typical next step. Priya will run a pilot with bench data and we'll set a benchmark harness.
05:20 Priya: One demo feature I want to highlight — the 'trace diff' view lets you pick two clusters of traces (good vs bad) and it highlights span-level deltas; e.g., cache hit rate difference, tokenization time, or kernel dispatch.
05:35 Marcus: Handy. If we see GPU scheduling as culprit can Redwood recommend autoscaler settings?
05:40 Priya: Yes, we provide autoscaler profile templates and tunables per model variant and volume.
05:48 Alex: Ok let's do a quick walk through request logs drilldown: searching for request_id 9f3a... there, shows full timeline and linked trace. Notice the header shows user_id but redacted.
06:00 Marcus: The transcript sometimes mislabels speakers; in our exports we prefer full names — can you include that?
06:05 Alex: We can. We'll send a naming convention guide.
06:12 Sana: Any limitations around sampling? We need 100% for a small pilot but not long-term.
06:18 Priya: You can do 100% sampling for a pilot, then step down to sampled rates for production. Storage cost and retention controls apply.
06:25 Jordan: Compliance: Do you have SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001?
06:30 Alex: Yes — SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in our compliance pack. We'll attach certs.
06:35 Marcus: Can you run a short end-to-end replay of a failing trace?
06:40 Priya: We can replay payloads into a sandbox lane. I'll demonstrate a truncated flow: selecting a failed request -> replay -> see the same 504 reproduce under a constrained lane because we limit concurrency. Reproduced.
06:58 Alex: That helps debugging.
07:02 Sana: If during pilot we find model-quality regressions after quantization, what's the rollback pattern?
07:08 Priya: Rollouts are canary-based; we support pinning model versions, automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to eval sets or prompt tests.
07:18 Marcus: Any tipping point where Redwood recommends Dedicated?
07:22 Alex: If you need guaranteed throughput and isolated capacity for p99 SLOs, Dedicated or Private with reserved GPU pools is recommended. We'll show throughput curves in the follow-up deck.
07:32 Ava: Who should we loop in from our infra to enable the pilot?
07:36 Marcus: I'll add DevOps (Samir) and legal for a quick REMSA.
07:40 Alex: Great. We'll share a pilot runbook.
07:45 Priya: Real quick: here's a case where the error analysis flagged malformed prompts causing tokenization explosion — the trace shows a sudden jump in tokenization time. We surface tokenization metrics too.
07:58 Marcus: That's been a sneaky one for us. Good to see it surfaced.
08:05 Alex: We're about halfway through — do you want to keep going into the deeper request log query language?
08:12 Sana: Yes please, show queries.
08:15 Priya: The query language supports filtering by header, model, span duration ranges, and custom fields. Example: model: "v3.1-quant" AND span.model_inference>2000ms AND header.request_id exists.
08:30 Priya: You can save queries as alerts — tie them to Slack, PagerDuty. Alerts can trigger sample replay or capture extra context.
08:40 Marcus: If we attach our existing PagerDuty, will Redwood dedupe alerts?
08:44 Alex: We recommend dedupe on Redwood side and then forward aggregated incidents to PagerDuty. We can help define thresholds.
08:52 Jordan: Anything else on security before we wrap?
08:55 Alex: We'll include SSO setup guide, KMS integration steps, and network diagram.
09:00 Marcus: Great. Let's recap next steps.
09:05 Alex: Recap: we'll send pricing + pilot template, SOC2 and ISO docs, run a pilot ingesting 1 week of request logs, Priya will set up tracing dashboard and bench harness.
09:18 Sana: Timeline? We'd like to start before EOY if possible.
09:22 Alex: We'll aim to kick off next Tuesday; Priya can start the bench config Friday.
09:28 Marcus: Okay thanks everyone.
09:35 Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack.
09:40 Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript: there are occasional mis-transcriptions (Nimbus -> NIMBUS, K V cache). Speakers sometimes abbreviated. Shared artifacts referenced: pilot-runbook.pdf (link to be sent), compliance-pack.zip (link), tracing-demo-recording.mp4 (link).
